description: Hi everyone! I’m a middle school student from Vietnam and the Team Lead of VN-Astrolab. I’m deeply passionate about space exploration, Earth science, and turning open NASA satellite data into interactive WebGIS tools. For this hackathon, we are building KRONOS-SIM—an interactive web platform
summary:
KRONOS-SIM is an interactive, browser-based WebGIS platform developed by Team VN-Astrolab to compare Earth’s volcanic and karst caves with lunar and Martian lava tubes using open NASA satellite data.

Space agencies rely on Earth-based planetary analogs to test rovers, sensors, and habitat concepts before launching costly missions, yet NASA’s planetary and Earth observation datasets often exist on separate platforms. KRONOS-SIM bridges this gap by integrating NASA GIBS and NASA Moon/Mars Trek via the open WMTS protocol into a dual-synchronized map. Users can side-by-side compare Vietnam’s Krông Nô volcanic lava tubes and Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng karst caves against lunar and Martian sites across four key parameters—mineralogy, terrain slope, surface temperature, and atmospheric pressure—visualized through a customizable Earth Similarity Index (ESI) and radar chart.

By connecting local geological wonders with real space science, KRONOS-SIM democratizes STEM learning and highlights Vietnam’s potential as a global planetary analog hub.
details:
1. What It Does & How It Works

KRONOS-SIM is an interactive, browser-based WebGIS planetary analog simulator that enables students, researchers, and space enthusiasts to compare cave systems on Earth—specifically Vietnam’s Krông Nô volcanic lava tubes (including Cave C7, the longest lava tube in Southeast Asia) and Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng karst caves—against subsurface lava tubes and craters on the Moon and Mars.

The platform operates through three core interactive modules:

  • Dual-Synchronized Map View: Displays Earth satellite imagery on the left and Lunar/Martian surface maps on the right. Panning or zooming on one map automatically synchronizes the other at matching spatial scales, allowing direct visual comparison of geological structures.
  • Quantitative Earth Similarity Index (ESI) & Radar Chart: Evaluates similarity across four scientific parameters derived from NASA remote-sensing datasets—Mineralogy, Terrain Slope, Surface Temperature, and Atmospheric Pressure. Each parameter is normalized to a (0-1) scale, visualized on a multi-axis Radar Chart, and aggregated into a single weighted ESI score.
  • Interactive Scientific Controls & Community Expansion: Includes a customizable Atmospheric Pressure Weight Slider an Earth’s Natural Limits disclaimer panel, and an + Add Analog Site feature that allows users to contribute and test new Earth analog locations.

2. Tools, Coding Languages, Data Sources & Software Used

  • Frontend & Web Mapping Engine: Built using standard web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript) combined with the open-source Leaflet web mapping library to render and synchronize side-by-side map frames directly in any web browser without requiring software installation.
  • Data Visualization: Chart.js (or custom HTML5 Canvas/SVG) to dynamically generate real-time Radar Charts and update ESI scores as users adjust parameter weights.
  • NASA Open APIs & Spatial Protocols: Connects directly to NASA GIBS (Global Imagery Browse Services) for Earth imagery and NASA Moon & Mars Trek for planetary elevation and surface layers via the international WMTS (Web Map Tile Service) protocol.
    • Mineralogy: Landsat / ASTER (Earth) and Moon Mineralogy Mapper ($M^3$) / CRISM (Moon/Mars).
    • Terrain Slope: SRTM (Earth) and LOLA / MOLA (Moon/Mars).
    • Surface Temperature: MODIS (Earth) and Diviner / THEMIS (Moon/Mars).
    • Atmospheric Pressure: NASA POWER (Earth) and Apollo / LADEE / Viking-Curiosity datasets (Moon/Mars).
  • Cross-Validation Benchmarks: Tested against established NASA planetary analog sites, including Krafla lava tubes (Iceland) and the Atacama Desert (Chile).

3. Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Zero-Barrier STEM Accessibility: Because KRONOS-SIM runs entirely in a standard web browser on laptops, tablets, or smartphones, middle and high school students can explore authentic NASA planetary datasets without needing expensive GIS software or high-end hardware.
  • Putting Vietnam on the Planetary Analog Map: Highlights the scientific value of Vietnam’s geological heritage—positioning Krông Nô as a premier basaltic lava tube analog and Phong Nha – Kẻ Bàng as a valuable control case for Martian astrobiology and GPS-denied autonomous rover testing.
  • Bridging Earth & Space Science: Encourages students to see local geology as a gateway to understanding planetary exploration, fostering environmental stewardship alongside space curiosity.

4. Creativity & Key Design Factors Considered

  • Scientific Honesty Through Adjustable Weighting: A major challenge in comparing Earth caves to the Moon or Mars is Earth's dense atmosphere. Rather than hiding this difference, we creatively introduced an adjustable Pressure Weight Slider and an "Earth’s Limits" alert box, allowing users to separate geological/structural similarity (lowering $w_4$) from true environmental habitability
  • User-Centered Simplicity for Young Learners: Designed with clean visual cues, intuitive sliders, and bilingual-ready terminology so middle school peers can grasp complex remote-sensing concepts within minutes.
